statement_blocker: The catalog gloss does not choose between surjectivity of a degree-g Abel-Jacobi map, an effective-divisor representative theorem, simultaneous Abelian-integral congruences, or an explicit theta-function inversion result. It also omits the compact-curve model, genus and connectedness conventions, symmetric product, divisor and Jacobian definitions, Abel-Jacobi normalization, ordered binders, exceptional cases, and relation to THM-M-0238 and THM-M-0240. domain_and_universes: Prospective compact connected genus-g Riemann surface or smooth projective curve X; a geometric degree-g symmetric product or effective divisors; first-kind differentials, periods and a Jacobian/Picard-zero target; and an Abel-Jacobi map. Exact universes, analytic or algebraic model, topology, genus, quotient, divisor, map, and normalization conventions remain open.
conclusion: Open. A modern secondary lead states surjectivity of X^(g) -> J(X); a fixed exposition lead describes simultaneous inversion modulo periods and an explicit theta-function route. The repository does not select which conclusion is canonical.
candidate_statement_shape_not_credited: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g. The degree-g Abel-Jacobi map from the symmetric product X^(g) to the Jacobian J(X) is surjective.
